description: start_session derives the new session ID from the request's idempotency key, so resending the same key does not start a second session while the server retains the runs that key may have started. Every implementation (TypeScript and Python launchers, the Go terminal UI and its tests) must turn each idempotency_key and harness into session_id, and must reject every invalid key. Hand-written; see agents/cli/TERMINAL_UI_CONTRACT.md.
rule: The key must be a lowercase, hyphenated UUIDv7 (RFC 9562): 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits, version digit 7, variant digit 8, 9, a, or b. Its first 48 bits are Unix milliseconds, which must lie from 2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z. session_id is <harness>-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>-<hex6>: the UTC date and time of the milliseconds floored to the second, then the first 6 lowercase hex digits of the SHA-256 of the key's 36 ASCII bytes. long_session_id is the same with the first 12 hex digits; start_session falls back to it when another request started session_id. Each start_session_cases entry lists the Flows the server retains, each with the StartFlow request ID that started it, and the ID start_session ends with: long_session_id when this key started it; otherwise session_id when it is free or this key started it; otherwise long_session_id when it is free; otherwise id_conflict. start_session_sequences apply starts and server purges in order; starts_new_run says whether a start creates a run. The guarantee that a resend never starts a second session holds only while the server retains the runs the key may have started.

vectors.description: 999 ms floors to the same second.
Same second as the first, other random bits: another suffix.
The last millisecond of a year stays in that year.
A leap day; the largest random bits and variant b.

collisions.description: Two keys of the same second whose SHA-256 starts with the same 6 hex digits.

start_session_cases.name: free
start_session_cases.description: Nothing has the ID: start it.

start_session_cases.name: resent
start_session_cases.description: This key already started the short ID: the same session.

start_session_cases.name: collision-falls-back
start_session_cases.description: Another key started the short ID: start the long ID.

start_session_cases.name: collision-resent
start_session_cases.description: Another key holds the short ID and this key already started the long ID: the same session.

start_session_cases.name: plain-chat-session
start_session_cases.description: A session the plain chat started, with a generated request ID, holds the short ID.

start_session_cases.name: both-taken
start_session_cases.description: Other requests hold both IDs: id_conflict.

start_session_cases.name: long-first-after-purge
start_session_cases.description: The short ID is free again (purged), but this key holds the long ID: the long ID, nothing new.

start_session_sequences.name: resend-after-the-other-run-is-purged
start_session_sequences.description: A holds the short ID and B falls back to the long ID. The server purges A's run, then B resends: B gets its long-ID run again, and nothing new starts.

start_session_sequences.name: resend-after-its-own-run-is-purged
start_session_sequences.description: Outside the guarantee: after the server purged B's own run, a resend of B's key starts a new session on the free short ID.
